candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108) (c. 100 BC)

'Woe to you who acquire silver and gold in unrighteousness and say: We have become rich with riches and have possessions; and have acquired everything we have desired. And now let us do what we purposed: for we have gathered silver, and many are the husbandmen in our houses' — woe oracle against acquisitive wealth. Direct verbal-thematic anticipation of the Lukan parable of the rich fool (Lk 12:16-21). Tewahedo monastic tradition of voluntary poverty roots theologically in the Enochic woe-oracle stream.
